name: Permanent Residence (Sections 26 and 27, Immigration Act 13 of 2002)

requirement_groups.name: Section 26(a): 5 years on a qualifying work visa, permanent job offer

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 5 continuous years holding a General Work Visa or Critical Skills Work Visa, plus a permanent (open-ended, no contractual end date) offer of employment from a South African employer in the same occupational category.
requirements.fix_path: Continue accruing 5 continuous years on a qualifying work visa and secure a genuinely permanent (not fixed-term) employment offer.

requirements.blocker_text: Foreign nationals with a Critical Skills Certificate, SAQA-evaluated qualifications, and at least 5 years' post-qualification work experience may apply for permanent residence directly, without first holding South African temporary residence for a set period -- see za_critical_skills_visa for the flagged discrepancy on exactly how this interacts with that route's own PR-eligibility claims.
requirements.fix_path: Obtain SAQA evaluation, a Critical Skills Certificate, and document 5 years' post-qualification experience.

requirements.blocker_text: Recognised refugees under the Refugees Act 130 of 1998 may qualify for permanent residence -- see za_refugee_status for the exact residence-period requirement, which this research pass found conflicting accounts of (5 vs 10 years) and left unresolved.
requirements.fix_path: Obtain recognised refugee status first (see za_refugee_status).

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a verifiable monthly income of at least ZAR 37,000 from a pension, retirement annuity, or guaranteed irrevocable income for life. This category is not restricted to retirement activity once granted -- holders may later engage in business, consulting, or employment without needing an additional permit, and holders can remain outside South Africa for up to 3 consecutive years (Section 28) without losing status, suiting dual/seasonal residents.
requirements.fix_path: Document verifiable qualifying monthly income of at least ZAR 37,000.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a verifiable net worth of at least ZAR 12,000,000, subject to a once-off, non-refundable fee of ZAR 120,000 payable to the DHA upon approval.
requirements.fix_path: Document verifiable net worth of at least ZAR 12,000,000 and budget for the ZAR 120,000 approval fee.

requirement_groups.name: Section 27(g): Relatives of a citizen or PR holder

requirements.blocker_text: Relatives within the first degree of kinship of a South African citizen or permanent resident -- parents, children over 21, and siblings -- may qualify, depending on the nature of the family relationship.

evidence_required.document: Form BI-947/DHA-947 (paper submission required for most categories)
Full set of fingerprints, police clearance certificates from every country lived in for 12+ months since age 18
Category-specific financial, employment, or relationship documentation

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: PR is revoked if the holder is absent from South Africa for longer than 3 consecutive years (Section 28), except where specifically exempted (e.g. the retired-persons category)

sources.title: Reproduction of official Department of Home Affairs (dha.gov.za) content -- Apply for a Permanent Residency, confirming Sections 26/27 structure and the refugee, retired-person, financially-independent, and relatives categories directly in DHA's own language
IBN Immigration -- Permanent Residence Based on Retirement or Financial Independence, describing Section 27(e)'s non-category-restricted post-grant rights and the Section 28 3-year absence rule

IDChecker -- Permanent Residence South Africa: How to Apply [2026], confirming the ZAR 37,000/month (27(e)) and ZAR 12,000,000 net worth plus ZAR 120,000 fee (27(f)) thresholds and the 27(g) relatives category
Migrate With Q -- Permanent Residence Permit South Africa, describing Section 27(b)'s Critical Skills direct-application mechanics and the 5-year post-qualification-experience requirement

notes: Six genuinely distinct qualifying categories, correctly modeled as OR-logic groups per this schema's core design decision, spanning work, skills, humanitarian, retirement, wealth, and family grounds -- one of the broadest and most varied PR-category structures documented in this dataset, comparable in scope to Saudi Arabia's Green Card tracks or Korea's F-5 sub-codes. dha.gov.za content was successfully accessed (via a reproduction site preserving the original government page's bullet-point formatting) confirming the core Section 26/27 category list directly, the strongest tier-1 anchor in this South Africa build alongside za_refugee_status's SAFLII fetch -- that fetch grounds the direct_work_based and refugee_ground groups specifically as hard:true. The remaining four groups' specific numeric thresholds (Critical Skills' 5-year experience figure, the ZAR 37,000/12,000,000/120,000 figures, and the relatives' exact kinship list) rest on tier-3 sources only and are modeled hard:false accordingly -- the category structure itself is confirmed tier-1, but the precise qualifying numbers for those four groups are not, an important distinction between confirming a category exists and confirming its exact current threshold. A real pending reform worth flagging for currency: multiple 2026-dated sources reference a government White Paper proposing to 'radically change how PR is awarded,' not yet enacted as of this research pass -- the categories and thresholds documented here reflect the current Immigration Act 13 of 2002 framework, which should be treated as subject to near-term change given this pending reform process. Processing-time reality is described inconsistently across sources -- official DHA targets of 8-12 months versus practical experience of 12 months to 2-3 years, a familiar backlog pattern also documented on za_general_work_visa and za_business_visa. PR status grants nearly all rights of citizenship (work, study, property ownership, social-security access, a 13-digit SA ID number with the identity-distinguishing 11th digit set to 1 rather than 0) except the right to vote in national elections and the right to hold a South African passport -- confirmed consistently across sources checked, worth surfacing as the precise practical boundary between PR and full citizenship in this system.
